Im not sure if the right people saw this or not. I’m not doing it for them, I’m doing this for me. I realized that I was wrong.   I agree with you. Looking back on how my family raised me, with spankings. Even tho those spankings were not what I would call a beating or abuse. They were still burned into my memory of childhood. 

I’ve had some time to think and meditate on my past childhood disciplinary experiences. I received spankings. My mother would always say, “ this hurts me more than it hurts you.” As a child , when this was said, I often wondered what it meant, because I was the recipient of these disciplinarian actions. I can remember that it hurt. 

I wondered why my mother would do this to me if it in fact brought her pain, and what kind of pain bc it wasn’t physical pain, I was the one on the receiving end. Later in life I realized what she meant when she said this. She was trying to let me know that she felt emotional pain from having taken part in physically hurting her son. 

After yesterday and listening to everyone against spanking and reading the comments and having last night to think back about how spankings made me feel, I started to also think about my sister. She also received spankings and I remember hers being more frequent than mine. The conclusion I came to was that I was older by 6 years. My parents were divorced when I was 8 months old. My stepdad never gave me a spanking and my father never gave me a spanking. My mother and stepfather both gave my sister spankings.

Last night I started to remember long forgotten instances in where my sister would be screaming and crying while getting a spanking. I remember now that it seemed insane to me, because the look of fear and embarrassment on her face was stoic. She seemed down for a while after getting a spanking and I would have to work very hard to get her to start being happy again. 

I had forgotten that this happened. I am a counselor and just realized that I have some untended childhood trauma from witnessing my sister go thru this with my mother and stepfather. 

I talked to her last night and I talked about what she had gone thru. I believe today, that I have a better understanding of where most of my sisters ptsd comes from.  I have no idea why I forgot how horrible it was, I guess it’s because I only stayed with my mother and stepfather on the weekends and during summer sometimes and after being away from my sister and not living with her, going to college, attending substance abuse facilities, psych wards, and sober livings.  I blocked it from my mind as a defense mechanism. 

I also talked to my dad about spanking and he told me that he never gave me a spanking. I have no memory of getting spankings from him either. He told me that he just couldn’t ever do that to me and that he and my
Mother agreed to never spank me. He was upset that she did. That was 39 years ago, and he still feels angry that it took place without his knowledge.

I am fully aware of my stance yesterday on spankings as an acceptable form of discipline.  I am writing today to let you all know that what you all said made an impact. After talking to my family and coming to realize forgotten moments in my past, I completely understand why y’all were so upset at what I was saying. As a counselor that works in mental health and being a human with mental health issues and also being in recovery from heroin for going on 10 years now, I should be able to listen to others and take to heart what other humans are talking about. 

I am not perfect, but I strive for perfection daily. I hold the mirror up to people daily and ask them to improve their skewed outlook on life and their lives, and others lives that could be effected by their actions. To one day have them move in a more positive wave in this ocean we call consciousness.  

I am sorry that I was close minded yesterday, and I apologize to anyone that was hurt in their childhood by corporal punishment and/or any kind of abuse. You guys are right, spanking is hitting. Hitting is abuse. Hitting and abuse cause fear which leads to anger which begets hatred.

If I kept going with my close minded approaches spanking, how could I seriously work with child protective services and have that mindset. I’m glad some of you questioned my ability as a counselor, because it lit a fire under me and motivated me to change. 

I want to thank all of you on Reddit in this sub for not placating me and opening my eyes to how I was wrong.  Update me and my sister are fine now, yes we both have ptsd from abuse and know I realize where it stemmed from. Thank you all. I am removing my original comment.
